calls.head: Don’t buy Lankinen’s slump against the Oilers
calls.body: Lankinen has been shaky against the Oilers since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.

calls.head: The Canucks can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Oilers’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Canucks’ kill is near the bottom. The Canucks need to stay out of the box. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

surprises.head: Kevin Lankinen got lit up
surprises.body: Lankinen allowed 8 goals on 20 shots, worth 2.5 expected goals: 5.5 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 2,500 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

surprises.head: Vancouver found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Vancouver usually gets some of the league’s least dangerous shots. Not tonight: a 9.5% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 5.9% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 80 games.

story.head: Five points for McDavid as the Oilers beat the Canucks
paras: The Canucks almost pulled off something wild. Devon Levi was back in an NHL net for the first time since Jan 20, 2025, and got the win. It was a busy first period. Vasily Podkolzin opened the scoring for the Oilers on the power play midway through the period. Owen Michaels, undrafted and in his second NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Mathieu Joseph, five minutes later to make it 2-0. Evan Bouchard stretched the lead to 3-0 just 16 seconds later. Ryan Shea scored his first goal for Edmonton with 28 seconds left in the first to make it 4-0. The second period brought seven goals. Leon Draisaitl stretched the lead to 5-0 just 27 seconds into the period, but Paul Cotter got the Canucks on the board just over four minutes later. Trent Frederic made it 6-1 for the Oil 33 seconds later. Brock Boeser cut Edmonton’s lead to 6-2, 43 seconds later. Connor McDavid and Kasperi Kapanen scored shorthanded 34 seconds apart later in the period to stretch the lead to 8-2. Vancouver pulled Kevin Lankinen after eight goals and turned to Leevi Meriläinen for the rest of the second. Arshdeep Bains made it 8-3 with just one second left in the second. The third period brought five goals. Marco Rossi scored twice and Elias Pettersson (#40) once in less than six minutes early in the period to cut it to 8-6. Draisaitl struck again on the power play less than two minutes later to make it 9-6 for the Oilers. Jamie Oleksiak scored his first goal for Vancouver with a minute and a half left to cut Edmonton’s lead to 9-7, and the Oilers had to hang on. McDavid finished with five points on a goal and four assists, and Draisaitl added an assist for a three-point night.

The Oilers had the better of the chances, outshooting the Canucks 31-22. The Oilers improved to 1-0-1, tied for first in the NHL in points. The Canucks fell to 1-1-0 in their home opener, slipping out of first in the NHL.

items.text: Elias Pettersson (#40) passed Bo Horvat for ninth on the Canucks’ all-time goals list, with 202.
The Oilers scored twice shorthanded in the second, their first time doing that since Jan 26, 2026.
Connor McDavid extended his point streak against Vancouver to eight games.
